findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan vent in the reach-in cooler by the handwashing sink was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The outer surface of the juice machine, especially the surface close to the orange juice nozzle was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The reach-in freezer between the reach-in cooler and Avantco reach-in freezer was observed to have ice build up on the wall surface.

The person-in-charge was instructed to have those surfaces cleaned by the inspector. Ensure the non-food contact surfaces are kept free of ice buildup and soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the standing cooler by the handwashing sink and milk cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

findings.citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: Observed floor base cove is pulling away from the wall in the area left of the dish machine. Repair or replace this cove piece. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the dish machine to be operating at 0ppm of chlorine sanitizer. The line to the sanitizer bottle was adjusted, sanitizer primed, and the machine tested at 50ppm of chlorine. The 50ppm is consistent with the machine data plate requirements.  The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to verify sanitizer concentration with test strips daily in both types of sanitizer used in the facility. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy at the facility. Facility has had a change in management since last inspection. Current CFPM/GM did not have previous paperwork. Provided copy of the Norovirus illness clean-up policy. Facility has bleach to perform procedure. No bodily fluid clean-up kit on hand. Discussed that if facility chooses, call EcoLab and they can provide a bodily fluid clean-up kit that will kill for Norovirus. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the paper towel dispenser next to the hand sink in the kitchen. Discussed with employee and CFPM/GM. Employee went to back to obtain paper towels. Employee was using reusable sani bucket rags to dry hands (clean rags). Ensure disposable paper towels remain at the hand sink during all hours of operation. COS.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed no CFPM present during breakfast service. Employee is only a food handler. The manager is the CFPM, not the normal worker in the breakfast area. A CFPM must be present during all hours of operation. Manager was not present during inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/17/2019.

findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114  (P) Quaternary ammonium sanitizer measured 0 ppm at three compartment sink and within sanitization bucket. Maintain concentration at 200 ppm to 400 ppm as indicated on manufacturer's label. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed 0 ppm in both the 3 compartment sink, as well as the sanitization bucket in kitchen. Discussed with PIC that all sanitization with quaternary ammonium must be between 200 and 400 ppm. EcoLab was called during inspection to repair sanitization of 3 compartment sink. COS. 

(REPEAT) 4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizing rinse at dish machine measured at 0 ppm chlorine concentration and 120°F. A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed dish machine to have 0 ppm sanitization level of chlorine bleach. EcoLab was called during inspection in order to service dish machine and repair proper sanitization level. Dish machine is in need of new parts and required to be ordered and serviced. Temporary procedure created to utilize dish machine to wash and rinse as the heat level is maintaining correctly, then utilize the quat at 3 compartment sink for at least 90 seconds submerged. Inspector will spot check dish machine on 12/26/2019. This is a repeat violation since last routine inspection.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Fan within kitchen is not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed fans within kitchen to have large accumulation of dust and debris. Discussed routine cleaning of fans with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles are stored incorrectly. Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

Observed multiple boxes of single-use utensils (protected within cabinents under service area) to have handles not aligned in same direction in order to hinder cross-contamination when reaching for utensils. Discussed with PIC.
